All operating notesOPERATING NOTE / 02

Keep the page reference beside the parcel decision

Plotmark editorial · 14 November 2026 · 4 min read

It prepares a due-diligence brief. It does not confirm ownership, verify a registry entry or replace a lawyer or licensed surveyor.

Start with the limits of the evidence.

An acquisition file can include hundreds of scanned pages and several versions of a survey. The AI must read the pages, match parcel references and compare conflicting details across the file.

Two questions need professional review. The report makes the conflict easy to locate without claiming that title has been verified.

Make the review practical.

  1. Match the parcel reference before comparing an area or boundary.
  2. Record the source version and date of each document.
  3. A missing file is an open question, not proof that the right does not exist.
  4. Use qualified legal and survey professionals for verification and sign-off.

One concrete example.

A survey lists 8.4 hectares while the title schedule, seven pages into another file, lists 7.9 hectares.

The prepared AI brief places both passages beside a 0.5-hectare discrepancy for professional review.

Ask the appointed lawyer and surveyor to reconcile the title schedule with the 8.4-hectare survey.

Keep the decision with the responsible person.

A lawyer, surveyor or acquisition lead resolves the question. It prepares a due-diligence brief. It does not confirm ownership, verify a registry entry or replace a lawyer or licensed surveyor.

The product’s sample workspace lets you follow that chain: source, finding, review and retained action. The example is prepared for demonstration and does not claim measured customer performance.
